children: The U.K. Competition and Markets Authority said it will investigate Bannatyne Health Club, Secret Escapes and Caledonian Travel over concerns about so-called drip pricing, or compulsory charges tacked on later to the headline price.
The CMA said the pricing model can leave consumers with unexpected extra costs.
The regulator said it has concerns that the companies added costs or failed to display extra fees during the customer purchasing process.
Secret Escapes and Caledonian Travel couldn't be contacted for comment. A Bannatyne spokesperson said the group noted the CMA's review and is cooperating with the process.

This is the latest move from the CMA to enforce the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act, a relatively new U.K. law designed to target unfair practices online and level the playing field in the digital economy.
The law bans drip pricing, and companies face fines of up to 10% of their annual worldwide turnover for breaches of the rules.
